what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: Three hours ago this project had a measured answer to the thesis and it was a loss. It no longer has one. `8b450a839` established that the per-customer arm's answers came from a bound because `renewal_margin_uplift`, its only production caller, passed six of `decide_margin`'s twenty company observables and let fourteen default -- and two of those defaults did the whole damage. The billed `revenue_gbp` includes the standing charge, so the arm compared an all-in GBP/MWh rate against a commodity-only offer and saw roughly GBP 55/MWh of headroom that does not exist on a small domestic account; and no ceiling reached the search at all, so the price cap landed afterwards as the fourth chain writer and `ceiling_bound` was structurally unable to fire. On one real account shape the chosen margin moved GBP 193.00 to GBP 60.00/MWh. That means the -GBP 93,555 net and -GBP 118,252 enterprise-value delta in `docs/observability/value_cycle_ab.json` is a measurement of a wiring defect and not of per-customer inference, and the same is true of the 20 ceiling cases, the 16 floor cases and the 27 cap clamps I read as the losing mechanism last night. The honest sentence is therefore not "the company loses to its flat rules" and not "it beats them" -- it is that the thesis is currently UNMEASURED, and knowing that is a step forward in epistemics bought at the cost of the only number we had. The confirming re-run has not happened: the parked record says it was started, no `value_cycle_ab_2026-08-26_observables_threaded.json` exists, no process is running, and the only new artefact is `value_cycle_ab_prior_2026-08-26T0802Z.json`, byte-identical to the 08:02Z original. Beside that, the belief half moved for real. `tools/couple_clv.py` was crashing on success, which had frozen EP1's coupled gap at a seven-day-old 1.7621 over five completed lives; repaired at `18e8d215e`, it re-reads 2.529 over 33 accounts -- mean belief GBP 473.71 against mean realised GBP 100.20, 27 of 33 magnitude-inflated, 7 sign disagreements, and one scalar absorbing four fifths of it in-sample. Above 1 means the per-customer estimate carries less information than handing every account the population mean, so on the one quantity every per-customer decision maximises against, the company is beaten by the crudest baseline available, and three of my own direction records reasoned from the stale 1.76 without noticing. On the previous focus the record is better than the brief says: all four items moved, and the brief credits only two because the two non-atom items were Lane 0 claims whose draw record is the very signal focus item two below exists to repair. The two stale BLOCKING findings are discharged and the register reads zero blocking. The value-arm diagnosis is finished. EP1's instrument is repaired though its estimator is untouched. And EP13 did not move, correctly: its own L2 ledger entry names three unmet L3 conditions, so my predecessor's instruction to move it was unsound and is withdrawn below.

focus.what: Run the A/B again on the fixed chain and read what it says. `python3 -m tools.run_value_cycle_ab --out docs/observability/value_cycle_ab_2026-08-26_observables_threaded.json` -- the `--out` argument exists (`tools/run_value_cycle_ab.py:317`) and writing beside the 08:02Z artefact rather than over it is deliberate, because the pre-fix and post-fix `decision_shape` blocks only mean something read against each other. If the run dies, restart it; do NOT re-diagnose the mechanism, which is settled and recorded in `docs/design/THE_VALUE_CYCLE_REALISED_AB.md`. When the artefact exists, read `decision_shape` against the pre-fix figures it must be compared to: `priced` 66, `endpoint_bound` 36, `endpoint_at_ceiling` 20, `endpoint_at_floor` 16, `distinct_margins` 36, `modal_margin_share_of_book` 0.2424, median chosen margin GBP 100.50/MWh. Treat `clamped_by_the_price_cap` as the control it now is: the arm searches under the same ceiling writer 4 applies, so a priced renewal that is still clamped means the two reads have come apart and that is a finding to file, not a number to report. Then `python3 -m background.delivery_lane --release value-arm-answers-a-bound` and archive `docs/staging/in_progress/WORKER_FINDING_REPEATING_ALARM_VALUE_ARM_CHOOSES_A_BOUND_NOT_A_CUSTOMER_WAS_CLAIMED_2026-08-25.md` to `docs/staging/done/`, naming the artefact that discharged it. Record the new realised delta whichever way it points, and do not adjust anything to move it.
focus.why: This is the acceptance test for the largest piece of work this project landed today, and without it the thesis has no reading at all -- the arm was fed six of its twenty inputs when the only number we have was taken, so both the loss and the shape of the loss describe plumbing. Every decision after this one is made blind until it exists: whether to fix the belief or the bounds, whether the value cycle is worth wiring, what Explore should be allowed to render. It is also the cheapest item on this list in judgement and the most expensive to keep deferring, because the stale artefact is the one the record, the site and my own last two orientations quote. Finished when the post-fix artefact exists beside the old one, its `decision_shape` shows where the arm's answers now come from, `clamped_by_the_price_cap` has been read as a control and its value explained either way, and the parked alarm is archived against it.

focus.what: Fix the delivery lane's progress signal so its pass branch can be reached, per `docs/staging/WORKER_FINDING_THE_DELIVERY_LANES_PROGRESS_SIGNAL_CANNOT_FIRE_SO_EVERY_LANE_ZERO_CLAIM_IS_RECYCLED_2026-08-26.md`. `background/delivery_lane.py:164` claims every Lane 0 item with `paths=[]`; `seat_work_in_hand._last_commit_time_touching` short-circuits to `0.0` on an empty list; so `moved > claimed_at` is never true and every claim is swept at `CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS` (100 min) regardless of what landed. The finding offers two shapes and does not choose; I choose LATE-BOUND PATHS -- the seat re-claims with the paths it actually touched as it lands each increment, since `claim()` already resets the deadline on re-claim and names that as the escape hatch, and it needs no change to commit-message convention. Do NOT restore the unscoped `head_time` comparison: that is the 2026-08-21 defect in the same module and trades a signal that never passes for one that never fails. Do NOT let the seat write a bare heartbeat, which is the tautology R15 names first. Ship it with the R15 pair the finding already specifies: a mutation proving the sweep still fires on a genuinely stalled claim, AND the null control proving it stays silent on a claim that landed -- the second is the one that does not exist today and its absence is why this shipped. In the same pass remove the residue the sibling "uncommitted work" alarm keys on, which is permanently true and so can never clear: the six `.land_*.sh` scratch scripts and `_r11_tmp.mjs` at the tree root, and the four zero-byte lock files `.tree.lock`, `.tree_lock`, `docs/.tree.lock`, `docs/.tree_lock`, all stamped 2026-08-20 with no live holder -- confirm each is stale before removing it.

focus.what: Find and fix the mechanism inflating three-horizon CLV magnitude in `company/analytics/clv_three_horizon.py`, using the newly trustworthy measurement rather than the stale one. `docs/observability/coupled_gap_ledger.json` at 08:07:31Z now reads mean belief GBP 473.71 against mean realised GBP 100.20 over 33 counted accounts of 263 available, gap 2.529, 27 of 33 magnitude-inflated, 7 sign disagreements, and `best_single_scale` 0.204 leaving `gap_after_best_single_scale` 0.806. Do NOT apply that scalar: the ledger labels it an attribution and never a correction, and applying it is a constant fitted in-sample to the exact comparison it would then be judged by. Read it as the diagnosis it is -- four fifths of the error is one systematic magnitude, not per-account noise, so look for a horizon, tenure or retention assumption that scales every account at once. Rule the ledger's own `truth_window_bias` in or out FIRST and say which it was: it records that realised spans the whole lifetime while the belief is the first year-end snapshot, which flatters an over-estimating belief and means 2.529 is conservative for exactly the cases that dominate here. Re-measure into the ledger afterwards with `tools/couple_clv.py`, which now exits cleanly.
focus.why: Every per-customer decision this company makes maximises against this number, the renewal arm above included, so an estimator claiming an account is worth roughly five times what the world paid is the upstream half of whatever the re-run reports -- and if the re-run comes back negative again with the bounds gone, this is where the answer is. A gap above 1 says the estimate carries less information than the population mean, which is the thesis losing to the crudest baseline that exists on the quantity the whole thesis rests on. It is also the first real lead this atom has had: five completed lives could not tell a scale error from noise and 33 can, and the reason we have 33 is that the coupler stopped crashing three hours ago. Finished when the ledger's next entry comes from a changed estimator rather than a changed sample, the record names the assumption that was wrong, the truth-window question is answered one way or the other, and belief and realised are read from the same book.

focus.what: Build the coupled-triad rung this atom is actually missing, then let the level follow the evidence. `sim/neso_carbon_intensity.py` already exists as the independent truth series -- NESO's published half-hourly number, deliberately a separate module from `sim/grid_carbon_intensity.py` so the two routes stay independent -- and there is no coupler for it in `tools/` (fifteen `couple_*.py` exist; none is carbon). Write it in the shape of its siblings, measure the gap between the company's reconstructed shape and NESO's published series, and write it into `docs/observability/coupled_gap_ledger.json`. The specific claim to test is the one `sim/grid_carbon_intensity.py` makes about itself in the L2 ledger entry: that its quietest half hours sit near 0.05 of average against NESO's bottoming out nearer 0.16, because no coal and no interconnector imports are dispatched, so any time-shifting benefit computed from it is an upper bound. That sentence was a recollection written in the grammar of a measurement; make it a measurement or correct it. Move `level_current` to 3 and self-certify with `record_level_up_self_certified` ONLY if the gap is measured and the atom's three named L2 reservations are answered -- and never `--no-verify` a `level_current` change. If the gap is large, that is the finding, the level stays at 2, and saying so is the deliverable.
focus.why: My last record told a worker to move this atom to 3 because its code had landed, tested and consumed. That was wrong on the atom's own evidence: its L2 self-certification states in its own words why L3 was not claimed -- an optimistic clean end, no Expert Hour, and the coupled-triad rung unmet for want of a truth series. The truth series has since been built and never used, which makes this the one atom on the board whose level can move on real evidence rather than on a landed file, and under the coupled-triad rule no world atom reaches L3 until the company has been tested against it and the gap measured. It is also the cleanest instance of the discipline the other three items are exercising: a number published without the independent comparison that could refute it. Finished when the ledger carries a carbon row produced by a coupler that reads both series, the 0.05-against-0.16 claim is confirmed or corrected in figures, and the level either moves with that evidence cited or is explicitly held with the reason.

what_next.why_this_is_here: Direction multiplies the draw's existing weights and can never zero one, so it can only ever be ignored -- never obeyed by force. Whether it was actually followed is therefore a measurement, not an assumption.
